newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmakers seek to cut acid rain emissions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmakers seek to cut acid rain emissions.

text.p: Legislation was introduced in both houses of Congress on Thursday that would halve the amount of sulphur dioxide emissions that power plants could emit as part of a package of measures aimed at curbing acid rain.

The legislation, introduced in the Senate by Republican Alfonse D'Amato and Democrat Daniel Patrick Moynihan, both of New York, would also put a cap on emissions of nitrogen oxides, which also contribute to acid rain.
A companion bill was introduced in the House of Representatives by Rep. Gerald Solomon, a New York Republican.
The legislation would also set up a NOx allowance trading system similar to one already operating for sulphur dioxide.

The bill would reduce NOx and sulphur dioxide emissions beyond the level presently required by the Clean Air Act in order to protect sensitive ecosystems such as the Adirondacks, Long Island Sound and the Chesapeake Bay.
